the spec holds speculative state -- it names 'branch_tag' -- but no algorithm unwinds it. An entry tagged with an instruction that never commits is never put back, so the table drifts out of step with the machine and stays there. Add an algorithm at /algorithms/- whose trigger names the flush, the squash or the mispredict, and whose pseudocode does the undoing: a loop over the affected entries that clears or restores them, saying which survive and which are discarded. Both halves are required. Adding 'or squash' to the trigger of an algorithm that goes on to do the ordinary update does not clear this, and neither does a body that only reads the entries. Where the paper declines to say what survives, choose a policy and record the alternative in open_questions: silence is not one of the options, because an implementer has to write something.
